title: Quantum Folding in Chebyshev-Based Quantum Subspace Diagonalization
summary: Quantum subspace diagonalization (QSD) with a Krylov space spanned by Chebyshev polynomials of the Hamiltonian is a natural ground-state method for fault-tolerant quantum computers, but every guarantee it offers---convergence rate, noise floor, and the cost of turning its classical output back into a physical state---is controlled by the overlap of the reference state with the true ground state, which decays exponentially with system size for any product state and non-trivial Hamiltonian.
